Package org.aristonis.diwan.database

Class ConnectionBuilder

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.ConnectionBuilder
public final class ConnectionBuilder extends Object
Configures and builds a root Connection; obtained from Connection.builder().

A name and exactly one driver source are required: driver(Driver), dataSource(DataSource) or connectionProvider(JdbcConnectionProvider). The other settings have defaults: an empty table prefix, bindings hidden in error messages, strict transactions on, and cleanup failures logged as warnings through java.util.logging, no listeners and a query log limited to 1000 entries.

A builder is not thread-safe. The connection it builds keeps a snapshot of the settings, so changing the builder afterwards does not affect it.

      public ConnectionBuilder connectionProvider(JdbcConnectionProvider provider)
      Sets a JDBC connection provider as the driver source.
      Parameters:
      provider - the provider, never null
      Returns:
      this builder
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if provider is null
      IllegalStateException - if a driver source was already set
      API Note:
      Use this to join transactions managed elsewhere, such as Spring's: a provider that reports them as external makes Diwan Database nest inside them with savepoints.

    • showBindingsInErrors

      public ConnectionBuilder showBindingsInErrors(boolean showBindingsInErrors)
      Sets whether binding values appear in QueryException messages.
      Parameters:
      showBindingsInErrors - true to append binding values to error messages
      Returns:
      this builder
      API Note:
      Bindings can hold personal data, which is why the default is false. The exception carries them in QueryException.getBindings() either way.

    • strictTransactions

      public ConnectionBuilder strictTransactions(boolean strictTransactions)
      Sets whether the root connection refuses calls from a thread that is inside a transaction it opened.
      Parameters:
      strictTransactions - true to refuse such calls
      Returns:
      this builder
      API Note:
      Such a call would borrow a second connection outside the transaction, so its writes escape the rollback and a small pool can deadlock. Switch it off only for code that writes outside the transaction on purpose, such as an audit log. The default is true.

    • onCleanupFailure

      public ConnectionBuilder onCleanupFailure(Consumer<Throwable> handler)
      Sets the handler that receives failures to give a session back after the work succeeded.
      Parameters:
      handler - the handler, never null; it may be called from any thread that uses the connection
      Returns:
      this builder
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if handler is null
      API Note:
      Such a failure never fails the call, because the work already took effect. The default handler logs it as a warning through java.util.logging.

    • listener

      public ConnectionBuilder listener(ConnectionListener listener)
      Adds a listener for the query and transaction events of the connection family.
      Parameters:
      listener - the listener, never null
      Returns:
      this builder
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if listener is null
      API Note:
      Call it once per listener; listeners run in the order they were added. More can be added or removed later through Connection.events().

    • queryLogLimit

      public ConnectionBuilder queryLogLimit(int queryLogLimit)
      Sets how many statements the query log keeps.
      Parameters:
      queryLogLimit - the most entries kept, greater than 0; the default is 1000
      Returns:
      this builder
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if queryLogLimit is 0 or negative
      API Note:
      The log is off until ConnectionEvents.enableQueryLog() is called; once full, the oldest entry is dropped for each new one.
